races.name: St. Austell Brewery Mares' Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Dunaden Island
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning from 40-day break under claim, suited by good going but trainer form poor

runners_data.name: Queens Up
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with unknown style but point form has substance, Brendan Powell booking significant
runners_data.comment: Runner-up in an Irish point in December and that form has some substance.
runners_data.spotlight: Second foal; dam a 2m hurdle winner; showed promise when third in December on second start in an Irish point (3m); that form has some substance with the fourth winning since; makes hurdle/stable debut but may find a couple too strong.

runners_data.name: Stavanger Rose
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with completion issues, has fallen/unseated in recent starts but trainer in good form
runners_data.comment: Yet to complete in four career starts and it's safer to look elsewhere.
runners_data.spotlight: Yet to complete in four career starts, pulling up in an Irish point and again on hurdle debut in February and she has since fallen/unseated midrace on latest two starts; it's safer to look elsewhere.

runners_data.name: Onefournine
runners_data.note: Confirmed front runner returning from 71-day break, neck second at Fontwell suggests retains ability
runners_data.comment: Disappointing latest but she's up in trip and sets the standard on earlier form.
runners_data.spotlight: Off for over a year after an Irish point win in 2024; built on hurdle debut promise when a neck second at Fontwell (2m2f, soft) in January before a disappointing run when favourite at Kempton the following month; that tempers enthusiasm but she sets the standard on earlier form and her pedigree suggest she'll be suited by the step up in trip.

runners_data.name: Jolissaint
runners_data.note: Prominent racer needing the run 30 days ago, last-fence point fall suggests ability but needs improvement
runners_data.comment: Point winner; entitled to have come on from recent hurdle debut after a lengthy absence.
runners_data.spotlight: Would likely have made a winning start in an Irish point nearly two years ago but for a last-fence fall; unsurprisingly shaped as though in need of the run when 48l sixth on last month's hurdle/stable at Chepstow (extended 2m4f, soft) after a long absence; entitled to have come on from that and could be an interesting contender upped in trip.

runners_data.name: Kaydence
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who was always out the back at Wincanton, bumper winner suggests better over hurdles possible
runners_data.comment: Fair bumper performer and her pedigree suggests she'll be suited by this longer trip.
runners_data.spotlight: Fair bumper winner who was always out the back when switched to hurdles and beaten 29l at Wincanton (1m7f, good to soft) last month; pedigree suggests she'll be well suited by this step up in distance and is one to take seriously.

runners_data.name: Bits Ballou
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who fades in finish, 40-1 on hurdle debut suggests limited ability currently
runners_data.comment: Hinted at ability on last month's hurdle debut but needs to improve for the longer trip.
runners_data.spotlight: Soundly beaten in a point bumper at Larkhill (good) in December and only hinted at ability when 40-1 for hurdle debut (2m, good) last month; needs to improve significantly for the longer trip.

runners_data.name: Laffer Curve
runners_data.note: Prominent racer in excellent form, third in handicap off 103 mark shows clear class edge in this field
runners_data.comment: Need to find a bit with Onefournine on the figures but should be thereabouts.
runners_data.spotlight: Has shown promise in three hurdle runs, producing her best effort on recent handicap debut at Huntingdon (2m4f, good) when third off a mark of 103; needs to find a bit with Onefournine on the figures but should be thereabouts.

runners_data.name: Davita Blaze
runners_data.note: Prominent racer from same stable as favourite, 20-day break ideal but limited form to date
runners_data.comment: Never threatened on hurdle debut and may be one for the longer term.
runners_data.spotlight: Well held in her bumper and, although shaping with a bit more promise, never threatened on hurdle debut at Hereford (2m4f, good) 20 days ago; goes up in trip but she may be one for further down the road; stable looks to have a stronger contender in Onefournine.

runners_data.name: Fountains Gala
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with unknown style, fades in finish and well beaten in both starts to date
runners_data.comment: Good jumping pedigree but it's hard to make a case for her on what she's shown so far.
runners_data.spotlight: From a good jumping pedigree but well beaten in her bumper and offered little encouragement again on last month's switch to hurdles; it's hard to make a case for her on what she's shown so far.

races.paceDynamic: Onefournine will take the field along from the front with Dunaden Island, Laffer Curve and Jolissaint tracking in behind, creating a measured gallop over this extended trip. With only one confirmed front-runner and several prominent racers content to sit off the pace, this sets up as a tactical affair that will quicken from the home turn. The lack of early pressure means Onefournine can dictate fractions before the prominent racers and hold-up horses launch their challenges. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can track the leader and have the tactical speed to respond when the pace lifts.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Tactical Battle Unfolds
scenarios.trigger: If Onefournine sets uncontested fractions and the pace only quickens from two out
scenarios.body: The measured early gallop allows prominent racers to position perfectly before unleashing their finishing kicks when it matters. Laffer Curve and Dunaden Island benefit most from this patient tactical affair.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Onefournine maintains her lead throughout and the chasers fail to close the gap
scenarios.body: The mare's class edge and tactical advantage of dictating terms proves decisive as she holds off late challenges. Her January Fontwell second suggests she has the finishing kick to repel challengers.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes too slow and a hold-up horse produces a late surge
scenarios.body: Kaydence or Stavanger Rose benefit from a crawling pace that sets up a sprint finish where their closing kick can be effective. The extended trip plays into the hands of patient hold-up horses.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Onefournine goes too slow early and gets swamped by multiple challengers
scenarios.body: The race becomes a messy sprint where any horse with a turn of foot can win, creating opportunities for outsiders. Chaos in the home straight favours horses with tactical pace.

watchPoints.text: Stavanger Rose has failed to complete in four career starts including recent falls and unseats
Onefournine returning from 71-day layoff after disappointing third start, needs to prove fitness
Queens Up has unknown running style and lightly raced profile makes her hard to assess tactically
Laffer Curve carries the highest rating and best recent form, likely to be prominent throughout
Kaydence was always out the back at Wincanton but bumper form suggests she can improve over hurdles

races.name: Newton Abbot Novices' Limited Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: No Panic
runners_data.note: Sole pace-setter after wind surgery improvement, can dictate fractions without pressure from fellow front-runners
runners_data.comment: Much improved after wind surgery when fourth at Wincanton 22 days ago; weighted to go well
runners_data.spotlight: Son of Nathaniel who was much improved on the back of wind surgery when fourth of 12 in 2m4f handicap at Wincanton 22 days ago; still lightly raced and weighted to go well (eased 1lb) over this longer trip.

runners_data.name: Bredon Hill Dart
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with crucial course-winning experience, may have needed recent Chepstow run after quick turnaround
runners_data.comment: Course winner; in good form until pulled up at Chepstow latest; worth another chance
runners_data.spotlight: Course winner who was in good form until pulled up in 3m Chepstow handicap 19 days ago; he may have found that run coming too quickly so is worth another chance in refitted cheekpieces.

runners_data.name: Albert Park
runners_data.note: Prominent runner struggling for form despite breathing operation, visor applied suggests connections still searching for answers
runners_data.comment: Is 0-14 and only tenth of 12 in Wincanton handicap 22 days ago; visor is reached for now
runners_data.spotlight: Is 0-14 and he underwent a breathing operation before coming in only tenth of 12 in 2m4f Wincanton handicap 22 days ago; visor is reached for now.

runners_data.name: Green Asset
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 149-day break under 5lb claimer, ex-Irish with solid Fontwell fifth form line
runners_data.comment: Not disgraced when fifth at Fontwell in November; no forlorn hope off a 3lb lower mark
runners_data.spotlight: Ex-Irish maiden hurdler who wasn't disgraced when fifth of 11 in 2m6f Fontwell handicap in November; no forlorn hope off a 3lb lower mark after a break.

runners_data.name: Masonbrook Meadow
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare with Exeter breakthrough win, returning from 125-day layoff under 5lb claimer Benjamin Macey
runners_data.comment: Off since a below-par fourth in handicap at Hereford in December; needs to bounce back
runners_data.spotlight: Gained her breakthrough victory at Exeter (2m) in October but she's been off since coming in a below-par fourth in 2m4f handicap at Hereford in December; she needs to bounce back.

runners_data.name: Makinbecon
runners_data.comment: Only ninth of 14 in Ffos Las h'cap for new yard two days ago; not easy to make a case for
runners_data.spotlight: Has offered little in his four runs, only ninth of 14 in 2m4f Ffos Las handicap for his new yard two days ago; not easy to make a case for.

runners_data.name: Gilded Glance
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner for Jane Williams showing poor recent form, needs significant improvement to feature

runners_data.name: Keepkalmandkarryon
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with consistently disappointing efforts, headgear suggests ongoing issues remain unresolved

runners_data.name: Jetty May
runners_data.note: Prominent runner for Paul Nicholls after breathing surgery, yet to transfer pointing success to rules racing
runners_data.comment: Placed in points but yet to offer much in five runs under Rules; tongue tied now
runners_data.spotlight: Placed in points but this Jet Away mare has yet to offer much in five runs under rules, undergoing breathing surgery before coming in last of 11 on her first go in handicaps at Taunton (2m3f) last month; tongue tied now.

runners_data.name: Tobi Kanobee
runners_data.note: Prominent runner failing to progress in handicaps, beaten 19 lengths when fourth behind No Panic at Wincanton
runners_data.comment: Has failed to kick on sent h'capping; needs to take a big step forward to get off the mark
runners_data.spotlight: Has failed to kick on sent handicapping, beating only one at Wincanton (2m4f) 22 days ago; needs to take a big step forward if he's to get off the mark at the seventh attempt.

races.paceDynamic: No Panic will be the sole confirmed pace-setter from the outset, with Albert Park and Jetty May potentially sitting prominent but both showing questionable early pace recently. The lack of genuine speed means No Panic can dictate comfortable fractions through the early stages without pressure. With most of the field preferring to come from off the pace, this sets up a tactical affair where the leaders can control the tempo until the business end. This pace shape strongly favours front-runners and prominent racers who can avoid the inevitable traffic problems that will develop in the closing stages when the hold-up horses try to make their moves.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Wins
scenarios.trigger: If No Panic gets an easy lead and maintains strong pace judgement
scenarios.body: The son of Nathaniel can dictate ideal fractions and prove hard to peg back, especially given his recent wind surgery improvement. The lack of early pace pressure allows him to save enough for a sustained kick when the closers emerge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Rush Succeeds
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes too slow and the track plays fair
scenarios.body: Bredon Hill Dart and Green Asset can time their challenges perfectly in the straight, benefiting from a sprint finish. The course-winning experience of Bredon Hill Dart becomes crucial in a bunched finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Albert Park or Jetty May can secure ideal positions behind No Panic
scenarios.body: The prominent pair avoid pace-setting duties while staying clear of traffic, allowing them to pounce when No Panic comes under pressure. Paul Nicholls' Jetty May could be primed for improvement after recent breathing surgery.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If the field bunches and multiple horses get hampered in the straight
scenarios.body: A horse like Masonbrook Meadow who finds racing room can capitalize while others struggle with interference. The 5lb claimer Benjamin Macey's positioning becomes crucial in a rough-run race.

watchPoints.text: No Panic could get too easy a lead if Albert Park and Jetty May fail to take him on early
Bredon Hill Dart may need the run after being pulled up quickly following his previous Chepstow effort
Green Asset faces a significant fitness test returning from nearly five months off the track
The 5lb claiming jockeys Shane Fenelon and Benjamin Macey could provide crucial weight advantages in a tight finish
Albert Park's visor application suggests connections believe there are still untapped reserves despite poor recent form

races.name: Thatchers Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Uncle Phil
runners_data.note: Front-runner returning from Willie Mullins yard under questionable circumstances, 26 days off and carrying 170lbs burden at age 9.
runners_data.comment: Hereford third offered some encouragement but he's failed to build on it; best watched.
runners_data.spotlight: Very well treated on old form for Willie Mullins, but he left that yard under a cloud and has yet to find any real spark since joining current stable; although his third of four Hereford (2m, good) in March did offer a glimmer of encouragement, he failed to build on it; remains with plenty to prove.

runners_data.name: Siam Park
runners_data.note: Confirmed leader with solid recent form including Plumpton win, Joe Tizzard's 2/25 record concerning but Brendan Powell booking positive.
runners_data.comment: Leading contender back over fences after two solid placed efforts over hurdles last month.
runners_data.spotlight: Four-time chase winner, most recently at Plumpton (2m1f, good) in November before falling in a Sandown Class 3 in January; returned from a break with two solid placed efforts in March over hurdles, latest when a close second at Taunton (2m3f, good) 21 days ago; switches back to fences in a very small field and should go well.

runners_data.name: Raffles Hermes
runners_data.note: French import showing improvement in Britain, will need to prove stamina at this trip against strong early pace.
runners_data.comment: Dual chase winner in France who is showing more of late and the better ground could suit.
runners_data.spotlight: Twice a winner over fences in France before joining current stable; made a low-key start to British career but latest two efforts have been promising, latest when a keeping-on third at Fontwell (2m2f, soft) in March; return to better ground could see him in a better light and he's one to consider in an open contest.

runners_data.name: Irish Chorus
runners_data.note: Only hold-up horse perfectly positioned to exploit pace scenario, Alan King 2/20 recent record worrying but Tom Bellamy rides.
runners_data.comment: Steps back into open company off 6lb higher but she remains open to progress over fences.
runners_data.spotlight: 2-4 since switched to fences, most recently against her own sex at Warwick (2m, good to soft) where the form has worked out well; steps back into open company off 6lb higher but she remains open to progress in this sphere.

races.paceDynamic: Uncle Phil, Siam Park, and Raffles Hermes will all want the lead, creating a fierce pace battle from the start over this 2m½f trip. With three confirmed front-runners in a small field, the early gallop will be strong and relentless, testing stamina reserves throughout. The demanding pace will set up the race for a closer, with the sustained gallop likely to find out any horse lacking full fitness or stamina. This pace scenario strongly favours hold-up horses who can sit off the pace and deliver late, making Irish Chorus the clear tactical beneficiary.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sustained Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If all three leaders engage in a pace duel from flag-fall
scenarios.body: The relentless gallop will drain the front-runners' stamina reserves, causing them to weaken significantly in the final half-mile. Irish Chorus can sit behind the battle, conserve energy, and deliver a decisive late challenge when the pace-setters capitulate.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Leader Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Uncle Phil or Siam Park manages to establish a clear lead while the others fight
scenarios.body: The dominant leader gets an easier time up front while the other pace-setters burn energy trying to get back in contention. The race becomes more tactical, potentially allowing a front-runner to maintain their advantage to the line.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Tactical Slow Start
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners surprisingly settle and don't engage early
scenarios.body: The pace becomes more sedate, turning into a sprint finish where class and current form take precedence. This nullifies Irish Chorus's tactical advantage and makes it a straight shootout between the best horses on recent evidence.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Pace Injection
scenarios.trigger: If the leaders go steady early but one kicks clear approaching the final mile
scenarios.body: The race develops into a two-phase contest with moderate early pace followed by a sustained drive. This hybrid scenario slightly favours versatile horses who can adapt their position during the race.

watchPoints.text: Uncle Phil may not handle the sustained pace battle given his age, weight burden, and questionable departure from previous stable.
Siam Park's jumping under pressure if challenged by multiple pace rivals early.
Irish Chorus positioning in first half-mile - needs to stay within striking distance without getting caught up in pace battle.
Raffles Hermes stamina reserves when pace quickens, having raced mainly over shorter trips recently.
How quickly the three front-runners establish positions - immediate battle suggests stronger pace scenario.

races.name: Tribute Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Striking A Pose
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who should track Lightonthewing but his 10-year-old legs may struggle to sustain a challenge over this extended trip
runners_data.comment: Offered a little more on latest start and well treated on past form, but needs to step up.
runners_data.spotlight: Five-time hurdle winner who hasn't looked like adding to that on recent efforts, although latest was more encouraging over C&D; well treated on past form but needs to step up.

runners_data.name: Welcheston Warrier
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suits if pace is strong but 38 days off and 0/7 trainer record this fortnight raises fitness concerns
runners_data.comment: Largely consistent and not yet fully exposed at staying distances; leading contender.
runners_data.spotlight: Ten-race maiden but, the Ffos Las blip in January aside, he's acquitted himself well in defeat this season and his recent form at staying distances has shown clear progress, taking another step forward at Hereford (3m2f, good) last time with the addition of cheekpieces, coping well with the quicker ground; leading contender.

runners_data.name: Lightonthewing
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner with 7lb claimer Ciaran O'Shea who won't overcomplicate tactics, 19 days since last run ideal
runners_data.comment: Effective in this sphere but yet to win off a mark this high.
runners_data.spotlight: Has more wins over fences, most recently at Exeter (3m, good to soft) last month under Ciaran O'Shea; failed to fire 20 days later but he's effective in this sphere as shown when a close second at Chepstow in February; yet to win from a mark this high but should be firmly in the mix.

runners_data.name: Dearkeithandkaty
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with highest class rating but needs others to go fast early to set up his late run, wears cheekpieces
runners_data.comment: Nudged up 1lb but the step up in trip with cheekpieces added could eke out improvement.
runners_data.spotlight: Off the mark at Musselburgh (3m, good to soft) in his third handicap, before two creditable efforts when finding one too good; the step up trip could eke out further progress, especially if the cheekpieces prove a positive addition.

runners_data.name: I Love You Sivola
runners_data.note: Prominent style with lightest weight at 142lbs but poor recent form and TV coverage suggests market confidence lacking
runners_data.comment: Hard to recommend on recent hurdle form.
runners_data.spotlight: Has had just the one win, gained in a French chase back in 2022, and there's little in recent hurdle form to suggest he's about to add to that; 6lb out of the handicap.

runners_data.name: My Own Lovely Lee
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning after 39 days off with 3lb claimer, cheekpieces added last time failed to spark improvement
runners_data.comment: Made little impact switched to a handicap latest and more is needed if he's to figure.
runners_data.spotlight: Has failed to build on early promise in maiden hurdles and made little impact switched to a handicap with cheekpieces added at Exeter (2m7f, good to soft) last month; more is needed to reverse the current trend and get his career back on track.

races.paceDynamic: Lightonthewing will dictate terms from the front with his natural lead style, likely setting a sustainable gallop over this extended trip without serious early pressure. Striking A Pose and I Love You Sivola should track in prominent positions, while the hold-up brigade of Welcheston Warrier, Dearkeithandkaty and My Own Lovely Lee will settle towards the rear. The lack of genuine pace pressure on Lightonthewing means he can control the tempo and kick clear late, making this a race that strongly favours front-runners and those who can track the pace early rather than hold-up horses who rely on a strong gallop.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lightonthewing Controls Tempo
scenarios.trigger: If Lightonthewing gets an uncontested lead and dictates a steady early gallop
scenarios.body: The 11-year-old can use his stamina and tactical advantage to kick clear approaching the final hurdle when others are struggling to close the gap. His recent Exeter success over 3m shows he thrives when allowed to set his own fractions.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pace Pressure
scenarios.trigger: If Striking A Pose or I Love You Sivola press Lightonthewing early and force a stronger gallop
scenarios.body: The increased tempo will suit the younger legs of Dearkeithandkaty and Welcheston Warrier who can use their class to sweep past tired leaders. Both have shown they finish strongly when the pace is on.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Slow Burn Tactical
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely with all runners content to sit and wait
scenarios.body: This becomes a sprint finish where Dearkeithandkaty's superior class rating (OR 104) and recent Musselburgh success can tell in a bunched finish. The O'Neill team's 3/29 recent record adds confidence.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If Welcheston Warrier or My Own Lovely Lee get the perfect pace setup with a strong early gallop
scenarios.body: The maiden Welcheston Warrier has shown consistent placed form and could finally break his duck if the race falls apart in front of him. His stamina looks assured at this trip.

watchPoints.text: Lightonthewing getting a soft lead - if he's allowed to bowl along uncontested he becomes very dangerous late
Dearkeithandkaty's jumping under pressure - needs to travel smoothly to deliver his class advantage in the closing stages
Striking A Pose's stamina reserves - his recent efforts suggest he may not stay this extended trip at racing pace
How aggressively the prominent horses Striking A Pose and I Love You Sivola commit to pressuring Lightonthewing early
Welcheston Warrier's fitness after 38 days off - any signs of rustiness will end his chances of finally breaking his maiden tag

races.name: Visit Kauto The King 6th May Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Tapley
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent runner whose Stratford win confirms current form and tactical speed to quicken off steady pace
runners_data.comment: Consistent 9yo who looks sure to give his running again despite the 3lb rise; respected.
runners_data.spotlight: Consistent 9yo who recorded his second win of the campaign at Stratford (extended 2m6f, good) last time, continuing a productive partnership with Isabelle Ryder; this drop back in trip shouldn't inconvenience and, despite a 3lb higher mark, he looks set to give another good account.

runners_data.name: Hold Up La Colmine
runners_data.note: Windsor winner returning after 31-day break but failed to progress since November success under same jockey
runners_data.comment: Hasn't progressed form a good start this season but a return to better ground may help.
runners_data.spotlight: Lacked fluency but created a good impression when winning at Windsor (2m4f, good) in November under Callum Pritchard; however, he's failed to kick on from that and returned form a break with a disappointing effort when beaten 33l at Fontwell (2m3f, soft) last month; return to better ground could help.

runners_data.name: Soldierofthestorm
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner with three chase wins this season but may lack tactical pace if pressed late
runners_data.comment: Up 5lb but he's made an immediate impact over fences and can improve further.
runners_data.spotlight: Three-time hurdle winner who has taken well to fences this season, building on an encouraging second on chase debut when scoring from the front at Sandown (2m4f, soft) in March, jumping soundly throughout; this represents a different challenge but the 5lb rise is unlikely to halt his progress and another bold bid is on the cards.

runners_data.name: Clotilda
runners_data.note: Paul Nicholls runner returning after 47-day layoff with mixed recent form but retains underlying class at lower level

runners_data.name: Sheldon
runners_data.note: 10-year-old in good current form whose Newbury second suggests stamina and jumping accuracy remain intact
runners_data.comment: Infrequent winner but running well of late and remains on a workable mark; player.
runners_data.spotlight: Infrequent winner, but running well since the turn of the year and his recent Newbury second (2m6f, good to soft) was solid; nudged up 1lb for that but he remains on a workable mark and is high on the list of dangers.

races.paceDynamic: Soldierofthestorm will take them along from the front at a sustainable gallop, with all four rivals content to track him in a prominent bunch rather than press early. The lack of genuine pace pressure means this will become a tactical affair decided by stamina and jumping accuracy over the final half-mile. Tapley and Sheldon have the best recent form and tactical speed to capitalize when the pace lifts. This shape strongly favours horses with tactical pace who can quicken off a steady gallop rather than pure front-runners or hold-up horses.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Tactical Finish Develops
scenarios.trigger: If Soldierofthestorm sets modest fractions and the field remains bunched turning for home
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint from three out with horses needing instant acceleration rather than sustained stamina. Tapley's recent Stratford win and Sheldon's Newbury second both came from similar tactical battles.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Soldierofthestorm builds an unassailable lead through superior jumping and stamina
scenarios.body: His three chase wins this season have all come from the front and the lack of early pace pressure allows him to dictate completely. The field fails to reel him in despite the modest early pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Late
scenarios.trigger: If the modest early gallop turns into a crawl with the field still tightly bunched at the last fence
scenarios.body: Raw speed rather than stamina becomes decisive in a messy scramble to the line. Clotilda's class and Hold Up La Colmine's November Windsor form could surface in these conditions.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Jumping Errors Decide
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses make crucial mistakes at the final three fences in the tightly-bunched field
scenarios.body: The race becomes about who stays upright rather than who has the most ability. Any of the five could capitalize if rivals fall or lose momentum through poor jumping.

watchPoints.text: Soldierofthestorm's jumping accuracy early - any mistakes will hand initiative to Tapley and Sheldon tracking behind
Hold Up La Colmine's fitness after 31-day break combined with inconsistent form since November Windsor win
Clotilda's position turning for home as 47-day absence may leave her needing the run despite Paul Nicholls booking
Tapley and Sheldon settling kindly behind the leader to preserve tactical speed for final half-mile
Benjamin Macey's 5lb claim on Sheldon potentially crucial if this becomes tight finish between top weights

races.name: Newton Abbot Open Maiden National Hunt Flat Race (Category 3 Elimination) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Taranis Dubh
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced with unknown style but Sean Bowen booking and 177 days off suggests significant expectation from Olly Murphy yard
runners_data.comment: Landed Irish point in October; son of Frontiersman must enter calculations for top stable
runners_data.spotlight: Half-brother to 2m3f/2m4f hurdle winner Jack Hoola; dam, placed in a bumper/2m hurdle, is closely related to 2m5f/3m hurdle winner Moyross, out of 2m/2m3f hurdle winner from family of high-class hurdler Minorettes Girl; landed an Irish point in October so this son of Frontiersman must enter calculations for top stable.

runners_data.name: Duhallow Storm
runners_data.note: Expensive purchase making debut for Anthony Honeyball with Sam Twiston-Davies taking the ride, breeding suggests stamina
runners_data.comment: 105,000euros 3yo; son of Walk In The Park rates an interesting newcomer for in-form yard

races.paceDynamic: Chocks Away is the only confirmed front runner in this field and should get an uncontested lead, setting a sustainable tempo over 2m1f. With most runners adopting hold-up tactics (Taranis Dubh, Ta Ra For Now Jack, Max d'Airy, Quickkick, Jubilee Jack, Gospel Moon), the pace will be steady early before quickening from 3f out. The lack of pace pressure means Chocks Away can dictate terms throughout, while the hold-up horses will need to time their challenges perfectly from off the pace. This race shape strongly favours prominent runners and those with proven finishing kick over genuine hold-up types who may find insufficient pace to close into.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Front Running
scenarios.trigger: If Chocks Away gets an easy lead and maintains rhythm throughout
scenarios.body: The Henrietta Knight-trained gelding can dictate ideal fractions and prove hard to peg back, having shown progressive form with a decent third at Plumpton last time. His prominent style perfectly suits the likely scenario of steady early pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closer Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes truly crawling and sets up for a sprint finish
scenarios.body: The hold-up horses get ideal conditions to unleash late kicks, with Quickkick's proven finishing ability and Max d'Airy's Paul Nicholls polish coming to the fore. Both have shown they can finish strongly when getting the right race setup.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Unexposed Winner Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If either Taranis Dubh or Duhallow Storm shows significant improvement from their limited starts
scenarios.body: The lightly-raced pair possess higher ceilings than exposed rivals, with Taranis Dubh particularly interesting given his sole start was on heavy ground. Both carry question marks but represent the biggest potential upside in the field.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Moderate Pace Suits All
scenarios.trigger: If Chocks Away sets reasonable fractions that allow closers to get competitive
scenarios.body: The race develops into a genuine test where both pace and hold-up horses get their chance, creating a blanket finish. This scenario requires perfect timing from jockeys and reduces the tactical advantage usually gained.

watchPoints.text: Chocks Away getting soft fractions early could make him very hard to peg back given the lack of other pace in this field
Taranis Dubh and Duhallow Storm both carry significant market expectations despite limited public form, watch for strong market moves
Max d'Airy going too freely early like he did in France could compromise his finishing kick in the straight
Quickkick needs to settle better than last time when wearing the hood for the first time at Taunton
The going remaining genuinely Good will suit most runners, but any ease in conditions could favour the unexposed French recruit Max d'Airy
